subject: Econ deep-dive: Skyline token velocity, burn range, and commitment options
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Vega <alicia@skylinelabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:13:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + ask: token velocity, budget bands, and preferred discount structure

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can come back with a tailored commitment proposal: 

Recap (from our notes):
- Skyline is building the real-time summarization/QA layer on top of customer call transcripts.
- Expected pilot in Q4 with a production ramp in H1.
- Sensitive customer data -> private deployment considered but initial evaluation on hosted API.

What we need to price properly: (short, actionable)
1) Expected token volumes (monthly) for pilot and 6/12-month ramp scenarios (please give low/likely/high).
2) Peak concurrent request profile or typical requests/sec (helps with Dedicated sizing).
3) Target unit economics: any $/1M-token target you’re trying to hit to make this viable?
4) Annual budget range for LLM infra for FY27 (ballpark is fine — we use this to show tiered options).
5) Any requirement that would push to Private/Dedicated (e.g., SOC2, VPC) during pilot vs prod.

Prelim notes on discounts we can explore (so you know options):
- Seed-stage starter credit (one-time trial credit + short-term promo)
- Committed monthly spend discount tiers (3/6/12-month terms) with steeper per-token savings at higher commit rates
- Multi-year incentive (rebates/credits tied to growth milestones) for mid-market commitments

If you can reply with the volume bands and budget range we’ll map to 2-3 concrete proposals (Starter, Committed, and Growth incentive) and attach a simple term sheet.

Attaching a blank NDA stub in case Legal wants to loop in — happy to sign.

Thanks — talk soon,
Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: Skyline_NDA.pdf (stub)
From: Alicia Vega <alicia@skylinelabs.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Skyline Labs Legal <legal@skylinelabs.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: token velocity, budget bands, and preferred discount structure

Thanks, Olga — appreciate the clear outline. Below are the numbers we can share right now (rough estimates, happy to refine):

Volumes (tokens/month)
- Pilot (months 1–3): low 1M, likely 5M, high 12M
- Ramp (months 4–9): low 20M, likely 50M, high 120M
- Year-1 steady state (month 12+): 80M typical, 200M peak for some customers

Concurrency / traffic shape:
- Typical requests/sec during business hours ~15–30 rps; spikes up to 120 rps during demo days.

Budget & unit-econ target:
- We’ve carved out ~$120k–$200k for infra/model costs in FY27 for this product line (open to staged commit).
- Internal target: we need to see <$900 per 1M tokens to be comfortable with the gross margin assumptions (lower preferred).

Compliance/Deployments:
- Pilot should be fine on hosted API behind private workspaces; production will likely need SOC2 + VPC connectivity within 6–9 months.

As for discounts — we’re seed-stage (raised $12M); a starter credit and a clear committed-use path would help accelerate a pilot to a paid pilot.

Next steps: please send 2–3 pricing scenarios and a short term sheet we can share with Legal. Also happy to do a short follow-up call Thurs morning PT.

—Alicia
Head of Product
Skyline Labs
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Skyline — starter credit / committed path — approval ask

Olga / Ben — quick internal: Alicia’s notes look like a standard seed-stage path. Recommend the following for the outbound proposal: 

1) Starter package (low friction):
   - $15k trial credit (hosted API) covering ~16–20M tokens of run-time depending on model; one-month validity for pilot only.
   - No commitment; objective is to convert to paid pilot by month 2.
2) Committed tiers (3/6/12 mo):
   - 3-mo commit: 10% off list on committed usage band
   - 6-mo commit: 18% off list, plus 30% discounted overage bucket for month-to-month spikes
   - 12-mo commit: 28% off list + milestone rebate up to additional 5% tied to 3 growth milestones
3) Multi-year incentive:
   - For true multi-year pledge (12–24 mo, min ARR threshold) propose an escalator rebate model (rebates paid quarterly as usage grows).

Ben / Olga — can you confirm we can extend a $15k starter credit here (seed-stage) and attach term sheet template. If yes I’ll approve for sales to send.

Karthik
VP, Revenue Operations
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Vega <alicia@skylinelabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: token velocity, budget bands, and preferred discount structure

Alicia — thanks for the detail, this is perfect and makes the math straightforward. Per internal alignment, attached is a short term sheet with three scenarios mapped to your low/likely/high volumes: Starter, Committed (6-mo focused), and Growth incentive (12-mo with milestone rebates). Key points below: 

Starter (Pilot) — no commit
- $15k trial credit (applies to hosted API usage)
- Covers ~16–20M tokens depending on model family
- Pilot support: standard onboarding + 2 office hours of architecture time

Committed (recommended for month 4+ ramp) — 6-month example
- Target commit: $60k over 6 months (roughly ~50M tokens/month at discounted rate)
- Discount: 18% off on-commit unit rate; 30% discounted overage buffer for spikes
- Early termination: pro-rata true-up

Growth Incentive (12-month)
- 28% base discount + milestone rebates (up to additional 5% back) tied to usage milestones at 3/6/12 months
- Option to convert to Private deployment quote once SOC2/VPC needed (separate SOW)

We’ve attached the term sheet (SKY-389-term-sheet-v1.pdf). If this aligns, can we do the Thurs morning PT 30-min call (I’m available 8:30–10:00 PT) to walk through the numbers and get Legal looped on the term sheet? Also, if Legal would like the NDA signed first I’ve attached our NDA stub signed by me.

Next step checklist:
- Alicia: confirm preferred scenario (Starter vs Commit vs Growth) and preferred date for Thurs call
- Skyline Legal: provide any comments on the attached term sheet or request redlines
- Redwood: we’ll prepare a draft invoice/commitment outline once scenario selected

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: SKY-389-term-sheet-v1.pdf (stub), Skyline_NDA.pdf (signed stub)
